Quick update from SRE after an initial sweep:

- Observed: large spike in KV backend latency specifically for the eu-west prefix namespace (prefix_id: eu-usr-75). The serving tier returned 502/504s and severe token-generation slowdowns when KV latency exceeded 200ms.
- Correlation: a background maintenance job started at 07:40 UTC to refresh prefix TTLs after a config push; the TTL refresh job inadvertently submitted parallel evictions across many hot prefixes, causing hot -> cold churn.
- Impacted path: prefix KV lookup (synchronous path) under the hosted runtime for medium-length sequences (512-1024).

Mitigation performed (08:05 UTC):
- Reverted config push that triggered the TTL refresh job.
- Scoped the TTL refresh to a smaller batch and throttled parallelism.
- Enabled per-prefix soft caching while the hot->cold pipeline warms back up.

Result: p95 dropped back toward baseline by 08:20 UTC; p99 improved but remained ~300–400ms above baseline for a few hours due to cache refill churn.

Logs (snippet):
"2027-05-10T07:40:12Z eu-west prefix=eu-usr-75 op=ttl_refresh evict_count=128 parallel=64 lat_ms=412"
"2027-05-10T07:41:09Z eu-west prefix=eu-usr-75 op=kv_lookup miss=true backend_ms=398"

We suggest the following next steps: live-roll forward a targeted cold-warm prefetch for the top 200 prefixes, add an emergency circuit-breaker to prevent blanket TTL refreshes from starting more than X parallel jobs, and run a short warmup load test. Engineering will prepare a patch for the TTL refresh orchestration.

-Laura (on-call SRE)

Elaine — quick update now that we've stabilized production.

Summary:
- Root cause: orchestration bug in the TTL-refresh job submitted concurrent evictions across hot prefixes in eu-west, causing hot-to-cold churn and a cascading KV latency increase.
- Fix deployed: orchestration patch to serialize TTL refresh across hot groups + emergency circuit-breaker to block >8 parallel refresh workers. Deployed 2027-05-11T14:10 UTC.
- Impact window: 2027-05-10T07:40–2027-05-10T08:20 UTC.
- Mitigation: rollback of the offending config, throttled refresh, soft-cache enablement, targeted prefetch for top 200 prefixes.

Customer outcome: we confirmed Glint's client-side metrics return to baseline and Glint's checkout funnel recovered; Marissa is working on the credits proposal for the business impact.
